 Jim Caviezel Breaks Silence on Not Returning as Jesus, Claims Devil Threatened His Life During ‘The Passion’
 November 6, 2026 
 By Jesse T. Jackson 
 Facebook X Pinterest Linkedin Email Copy URL 
 Raymond Arroyo interviewing Jim Caviezel. Screengrab via YouTube / Raymond Arroyo 
 Share
 Facebook X Pinterest Linkedin Email Copy URL 
 Actor Jim Caviezel, who portrayed Jesus Christ in Mel Gibson’s 2004 film “ The Passion of the Christ ,” recently expressed disappointment after not being cast to reprise the Jesus role in Gibson’s upcoming “ The Resurrection of the Christ ” films.
 During an interview with Raymond Arroyo, Caviezel also recalled an encounter he had with the devil while filming “The Passion of the Christ.”
 After Arroyo pointed out that audiences had expected Caviezel to return as Jesus for nearly two decades, he asked the actor what happened.
 “Well, honestly, I read the first and the second script,” Caviezel said. “And Jesus really is not—he really didn’t need me. It’s a smaller role.”
 RELATED: Finnish Actor Jaakko Ohtonen Will Replace Jim Caviezel as Jesus in Sequel to Mel Gibson’s ‘The Passion of the Christ’ 
 Caviezel compared the role of Jesus in the upcoming films to his leading role in “The Passion of the Christ” and his work in other projects.
 “Good luck to the new guy, cuz it’ll be really hard,” he said. “As I said earlier, it’s a hell of a lot harder to play Jesus than Superman.”
 The actor expressed confidence in the lasting impact of his portrayal of Christ.
 “What we did on that movie, they can’t touch it,” Caviezel said. “Nothing. When I’m dead and gone, that’s an annuity. People are going to keep coming back and finding God. And I did my job and I did it well.”
 RELATED: ‘It Will Be the Biggest Film in History’—Jim Caviezel Says ‘The Passion of the Christ’ Sequel Could Be 2 Movies 
 When Arroyo suggested that returning to portray Jesus would have prevented Caviezel from working on his other films, the actor agreed.
 “No, I couldn’t have done it. I couldn’t have done these films,” Caviezel said. “But did I want to do it? Of course I did,” he said.
 Caviezel stars in “ Ghost Soldier ” and Angel Studio’s “ Zero A.D. ,” both of which release in the finals two months of the year.
